q: In his letter, James says faith by itself, without action, is what?
why: Real faith shows itself in deeds.
quote: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

q: James asks about a brother or sister lacking clothes and what?
why: Words alone do not feed anyone.
quote: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.

q: In James, what is wrong with saying, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed”?
quote: but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?

q: In James, how does a believer show his faith?
quote: and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

q: In James, which father is said to show faith by offering his son on the altar?
why: His faith worked with his actions.
quote: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

q: In James, what was Abraham called because his faith was real?
quote: and he was called a friend of God.

q: In James, which woman showed her faith by welcoming the spies?
quote: was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies

q: In James, faith without deeds is dead, just as the body without what?
quote: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

q: In his letter, James says to consider it pure joy when you face what?
quote: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds

q: In James, if anyone lacks wisdom, what should he do?
quote: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God

q: In James, the one who doubts is like what?
why: He is tossed by the wind.
quote: because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

q: In James, everyone should be quick to listen and slow to do what?
quote: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger

q: In James, believers are told to be doers of the word, not only what?
quote: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.

q: In James, a small spark setting a great forest ablaze is like what?
why: Small words can do great harm.
quote: the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things.

q: In James, what happens when you resist the devil?
quote: Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

q: In James, what does God do when you draw near to Him?
quote: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.

q: In James, life is compared to what, which appears and then vanishes?
quote: You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

q: To whom did James address his letter?
why: He wrote to believers in the Dispersion.
quote: To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.

q: In James, which prophet prayed and no rain fell for three and a half years?
why: He was a man just like us.
quote: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain

q: In James, who also believe that God is one, and shudder?
why: Belief alone is not saving faith.
quote: Even the demons believe that—and shudder.

q: In James, what does he say no man can tame?
why: It is full of deadly poison.
quote: but no man can tame the tongue.

q: In James, what kind of person's prayer has great power to prevail?
quote: The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
